dedupe_keys.name: federal reserve supervisory stress test scenarios and results dfast

description: The Federal Reserve's supervisory stress tests evaluate how a hypothetical severe recession would affect the capital ratios of large US banks, and the Board publishes the scenarios, model documentation and bank-level results each year. It is produced by the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System under the Dodd-Frank Act. The 2026 exercise used a baseline, a supervisory severely adverse scenario and a severely adverse global market shock, each defined by domestic and international variables over a nine-quarter horizon; results were released on 24 June 2026, and historical exercises and CCAR material from 2011 to 2021 are archived. Scenario paths are free CSV files with data dictionaries, market shocks are Excel files, and documentation such as the macroeconomic model guide is PDF. Caveats: scenarios are hypothetical designs, not forecasts, and results feed capital rules through the stress capital buffer, so the method changes between years; the pages read give no licence statement. For simulation it offers ready-made stress paths for unemployment, rates, asset prices and other variables that resilience and cascading failure models of banks and infrastructure finance can reuse. It is related to the EBA EU-wide stress testing record in this catalogue, the European counterpart.
